papers.title: Forest pest prediction using a hybrid Random Forest–LSTM model
papers.authors: Jiaqi Xu, Jiaqi Zhang, Xiumei Mo, Guofei Fang, Chengdong Xu
papers.abstract: Introduction Forest pest outbreaks can substantially affect forest ecosystem stability and pose challenges to forest health monitoring and risk management. However, forest pest monitoring datasets commonly contain a high proportion of zero observations and exhibit pronounced temporal variability, which can limit the predictive performance of conventional machine learning approaches. To address these challenges, this study developed a hybrid RF-LSTM framework incorporating Zero-Inflated Poisson (ZIP) features and LSTM-derived temporal features to evaluate the effects of these feature enhancements on Random Forest (RF) model performance. Methods Multi-station daily monitoring data for Coleoptera and Lepidoptera in Rui’an City, Zhejiang Province, China, were used to evaluate the proposed framework. The ZIP model was first employed to characterize the zero inflation structure of pest occurrence data, while the LSTM network was used to extract temporal representations from sequences of meteorological, seasonal, and ZIP-derived features. The ZIP-derived and LSTM-derived features were then incorporated into the RF model for evaluation. Results Compared with the conventional RF model, inco

papers.title: Emerging threat of Liriomyza spp. (Agromyzidae, Diptera) in horticultural crops: Species distribution, habitat shift and its semiochemical-based management strategies
papers.authors: S Renuga, Elaiyabharathi Thiyagarajan, M Karthikeyan, Srinivasan Govindaraj, Haripriya Shanmugam
papers.abstract: The genus Liriomyza (Diptera: Agromyzidae) has recently gained a reputation as a highly invasive and damaging leafminers group causing heavy economic damage in horticultural crops globally. The rising pest status of Liriomyza species is linked to climate change, protected cultivation, agricultural intensification, globalisation and movement of infested planting material, resulting in rapid geographic spread and host range expansion. The overreliance on broad-spectrum insecticides has led to insecticide resistance, pest resurgence, imbalance of predator-prey population dynamics and environmental pollution, thus making eco-friendly control approaches imperative. Among such approaches, kairomone and herbivore-induced plant volatiles (HIPVs) based strategies appear as very promising tools for species-specific monitoring and pest management. The current review provides an overview of the recent research on Liriomyza species diversity, invasion history, biology, adaptations to new environments, as well as morphological and molecular taxonomy. papers.title: An agent-based model of insecticide resistance in the Brown planthopper : comparing spray strategies in Mekong Delta rice [résumé]
papers.authors: J.M. Cabatingan, A. Brugière, P. Taillandier, Tri Nguyen-Huu, Alexis Drogoul
papers.abstract: As the main rice-producing region of Vietnam, the Mekong Delta depends on intensive, continuous cropping that providespests with a host almost year-round. The brown planthopper (Nilaparvata lugens) is one of its most damaging pests. Duringthe 2006-2007 outbreak, the planthopper and the viruses it carries damaged about 485,000 ha and destroyed about 828,000 tof rice (Heong et al., 2015). Farmers often manage it by spraying insecticides on a fixed schedule. However, the planthopperhas developed resistance to several insecticides, with higher resistance levels reported in the Mekong Delta than in northernVietnam (Khoa et al., 2018). Moreover, a survey of more than 5,000 households found that more frequent spraying did notgenerally increase yield (Heong et al., 2015). We develop a pest-management agent-based model to analyze how spray frequency and insecticide choice affect rice yield and farm profit as resistance builds up. The model extends STAR-FARM, an agent-based model of the Mekong Delta thatcouples farmer decision-making with a crop model (Taillandier et al., under review), and supports the analysis of transitionstowards more sustainable practices, including those promoted by Vi

papers.title: Advances in integrated wheat disease management
papers.source: OpenAlex / Burleigh Dodds series in agricultural science
papers.abstract: Wheat is one of the world’s most important crops and is a staple ingredient in the diets of millions of people around the world. However, it’s been estimated that around 20% of global wheat yields are lost to pests and diseases each year. As the agricultural sector faces growing pressure to reduce its reliance on chemical inputs, the development of integrated disease management programmes is gaining momentum as a sustainable alternative. Advances in integrated wheat disease management provides a comprehensive overview of recent developments in understanding and monitoring major diseases affecting wheat, as well as methods for developing fungal and bacterial disease-resistant wheat varieties. The book also reviews the range of integrated management techniques used to prevent and/or control disease outbreaks, such as the use of bioprotectants, intercropping and crop rotations. The book builds on a successful earlier volume published by Burleigh Dodds Science: Integrated disease management of wheat and barley (2018).

papers.title: Validating regional insect pest phenology forecasts using published developmental data
papers.authors: Darío San Segundo Molina, Constantí Stefanescu, Ignacio Morales‐Castilla
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Crop losses caused by insect pests are expected to increase under global warming, highlighting the need for accurate phenology forecasts to support integrated pest management (IPM). Arthropod pests, as ectotherms, exhibit temperature-dependent development and phenology that can be described by thermal performance curves (TPCs). For decades, developmental models have predicted pest emergence through thermal accumulation approaches, yet it remains unclear to what extent experimentally derived development models can accurately predict field phenology across spatial and temporal scales. Here, we evaluate whether developmental TPCs and linear degree-day models fitted from published experimental data can predict large-scale pest phenology under a rate-summation approach. RESULTS: We compiled published developmental data for the widespread crucifer pest Pieris rapae and fitted several TPCs and linear degree-day models. Model predictions were validated against independent long-term monitoring data from the Catalan Butterfly Monitoring Scheme for mainland Spain and the Balearic Islands. papers.title: Plant disease detection and recognition using hyperspectral remotely sensed data: A review
papers.authors: Subramanian Vishalini, Ramalingam Kumaraperumal, Ramasamy Jagadeeswaran, Karuppusamy Sivasubramanian, Kavitha Saravanakumar
papers.abstract: Plant diseases are an inevitable challenge in agricultural production, yet timely intervention and effective management practices can significantly prevent crop losses and sustain yield and quality. Conventional diagnostic approaches depend on visual evaluation and labour-intensive, time-consuming physical sample collection, making them inadequate for large-scale crop monitoring and often detecting diseases only after visible symptoms appear, considerably hampering the potential for early disease detection. These limitations necessitate unbiased and automated approaches to disease monitoring and diagnosis. By measuring spectral reflectance across hundreds of continuous wavelength bands in the visible, near-infrared (NIR) and shortwave infrared (SWIR) domains, hyperspectral remote sensing represents a revolutionary technique facilitating non-invasive, spatially comprehensive crop health assessment. Disease-related physiological and metabolic changes such as chlorophyll loss, water stress and pigment alteration generate distinctive spectral signatures detectable by hyperspectral sensors with high resolution. papers.title: Major outbreaks of listeriosis caused by consuming animal-derived products in Europe during the past 15 years: A review
papers.authors: Bianca Luisa Ghițan, Adriana Morar, Sebastian Alexandru Popa, Răzvan-Tudor Pătrînjan, Alexandra Pocinoc
papers.source: OpenAlex / Romanian Journal of Veterinary Sciences
papers.abstract: Listeriosis, a severe foodborne disease primarily caused by Listeria monocytogenes, continues to pose a major public health challenge in Europe, particularly among pregnant women, elderly individuals, and immunocompromised patients. Despite advancements in food safety and monitoring systems, the incidence of invasive human listeriosis has shown an upward trend in the last fifteen years. This review synthesizes recent epidemiological evidence and outbreak data from 2010 to 2024, emphasizing large-scale events associated with animal-derived and ready-to-eat (RTE) foods such as meat, fish, and dairy products. Notable outbreaks include those linked to blood sausage in Germany (2018–2019; 112 cases), stuffed pork in Spain (2019; 207 cases), and smoked fish products in Denmark and Switzerland. The persistence and recurrence of L. monocytogenes within food-processing environments, facilitated by its ability to survive at low temperatures, tolerate salt and acidity, and form biofilms on industrial surfaces, underscore the difficulty of eradicating this pathogen from the food chain. papers.title: Profiling insecticide resistance in Anopheles gambiae s.l. and Anopheles stephensi from Kenya using in-country nanopore sequencing
papers.authors: Cynthia Awuor Odhiambo, Sylvia Milanoi, Karolina Glanz, Diana Omoke, Cyprian Adala
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Malaria remains a threatening disease in Kenya, with over 70% of the population at risk of getting infected. Although vector control interventions such as indoor residual spraying and insecticide treated nets have significantly reduced transmission, the emergence of insecticide resistance and spread of invasive species such as Anopheles stephensi threaten these gains. This emphasizes the need for continuous insecticide resistance monitoring to inform NMCPs on the selection and deployment of effective vector control tools. Therefore, we developed a simple and cost-effective nanopore sequencing insecticide resistance method that targets key insecticide resistant markers, including target site (Vgsc, Gaba receptor ) and metabolic resistance markers ( Ace1 and Gste2 ). Results The panel achieved a mean sequencing depth of > 1,000 for most targets and was able to define the resistance profiles of 69/70 (98%) An. gambiae s.s , 45/48 (94%) An. arabiensis and 63/80 (79%) An. stephens i isolates collected across Kenya. The KDR East ( Vgsc L995S) mutation was at a high frequency in An. gambiae s.s (85%) but at low frequencies in both An. stephensi (5%) and An. arabiensis

papers.title: Neonic stewardship for MED Bemisia tabaci management: evaluating insecticide alternatives and biological control compatibility in greenhouse ornamentals
papers.authors: Vivek Jha, Garima Kakkar, Subash Dahal, Lance S. Osborne, Cindy L. McKenzie
papers.abstract: Invasive Mediterranean Bemisia tabaci (MED, biotype Q) is a major pest in greenhouse ornamental production because repeated insecticide use has increased reliance on neonicotinoids and intensified concern about resistance and long-term control failure. This study evaluated a neonic stewardship approach for MED whitefly management by comparing selected conventional and non-neonic insecticides for efficacy against MED whitefly life stages and for compatibility with the predatory mite Amblyseius swirskii , a widely used biological control agent in protected crops. Experiments were conducted on potted salvia under greenhouse cage conditions using four treatments: untreated control, insecticide alone, A. swirskii alone, and A. swirskii + insecticide. Across the 8-week study period, dinotefuran, cyantraniliprole, pyrifluquinazon, flupyradifurone, spinetoram + sulfoxaflor, and afidopyropen reduced MED whitefly populations, whereas pymetrozine provided comparatively weak and inconsistent suppression. papers.title: PCR-based assays for determining mating status in field-weathered Ceratitis capitata with enhanced precision across conventional, quantitative, and droplet digital platforms
papers.authors: José Marcelino, Cameron Zuck, Héctor Urbina, Matthew R. Moore, Matthew S. Siderhurst
papers.abstract: Accurately determining the mating status of the agricultural fruit fly pest Ceratitis capitata , commonly known as Medfly, is essential for timely and effective eradication efforts. To overcome the limitations of subjective DAPI-based staining assessments of females captured in dry Jackson traps and liquid Multilure traps, we developed a multi-tier molecular diagnostic method that unequivocally detects mating status using DNA probes targeting the male-specific Y114 locus on the Y-chromosome of C. capitata . Our protocol integrates morphological evaluation with increasingly sensitive molecular assays through the following steps: (1) A preliminary quality assessment of the specimens’ physical condition, DNA preservation, and mating status using conventional polymerase chain reaction (PCR) followed by agarose electrophoresis (cPCR); (2) quantification and real-time detection of sperm presence via quantitative PCR (qPCR); and (3) detection of trace amounts of sperm through droplet digital PCR (ddPCR). papers.title: Prevention of Destructive Fishing in the Waters of Tual City: Effective Surveillance and Law Enforcement Strategies
papers.authors: Suharta ., Sigit Bintoro, Riyan Maulana, Ismi Isti Anah
papers.source: Crossref / International Journal of Multidisciplinary Research and Growth Evaluation
papers.abstract: <jats:p>Destructive fishing in the waters of Tual City remains a significant environmental and socio-economic issue, threatening marine biodiversity and the livelihoods of local fishermen. This study analyzes the problem using a SWOT approach, identifying strengths such as existing government regulations and rich marine resources, weaknesses including limited enforcement capacity and economic dependence on harmful fishing practices, opportunities such as growing global demand for sustainable seafood, and threats like illegal fishing and climate change. Based on the SWOT analysis, several policy recommendations are proposed, including strengthening law enforcement, promoting sustainable alternative livelihoods, enhancing education and awareness programs, expanding marine protected areas (MPAs), and creating market incentives for responsible fisheries. These strategies aim to transition Tual City towards sustainable fisheries management, balancing environmental conservation with economic development. Effective implementation of these policies will not only mitigate destructive fishing but also ensure long-term resilience for both the ecosystem and local fishing communities.</jats:p>

papers.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Investigating human health during work importantly affect the safety and efficiency of the society. Different types of activity, including industrial, constructional, heavy duty ones, etc., affect the health of workers during their activities. In this study, the Multi-Objective Decision-Making (MODM) method was combined with fuzzy TOPSIS to investigate and optimize the air pollution risk affecting the health and safety of construction workers of Lar City, Fars Province, Iran. Methods: The comparison matrices (binary) and the Phillips–Perron test of different criteria and sub-criteria of health risk, including safety view, safety efficiency, understanding the risk, and risk investigation, were assessed to find the most influential factors for the optimization of the health risk of the workers. Results: Accordingly, the results indicated that “understanding the risk” followed by “safety efficiency” affected the health risk of the construction workers the most. papers.source: Crossref / Journal of Advances in Environmental Health Research
papers.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Population growth, numerous factories, and many vehicles are the primary sources of environmental pollution and toxic elements in the industrial city of Arak, Iran. Methods: In June 2016, a total of 30 toxic element samples were taken from surface soils to examine their contents of lead (Pb), Zinc (Zn), Copper (Cu), Nickel (Ni), Arsenic (As), Chromium (Cr), and Cadmium (Cd). The samples were collected from 0 to 20 cm depth and measured using Atomic Absorption Spectroscopy (AAS) (PG990 Model). Results: The results showed that the mean concentrations of all toxic elements except arsenic had a higher value than the background values in the world. The Top Enrichment Factor (TEF) of toxic elements of nickel, chromium, lead, and copper was higher than other elements. The Potential Ecological Risk (PER) index showed high and very high risk for the elements. For all elements, the Hazard Index (HI) values were higher for children than for adults. papers.title: Utilizing the invasive fruitwood Pyrus calleryana as substrate for mushroom cultivation, an experimental study in practical sustainability
papers.authors: Matthew D Helton
papers.source: OpenAlex / UTC Scholar (University of Tennessee at Chattanooga)
papers.abstract: This study evaluated the feasibility of using woodchips from the invasive Pyrus calleryana (Callery pear) as substrate for mushroom cultivation. Pleurotus ostreatus, Hericium erinaceus, and Ganoderma lucidum were grown on a pear wood substrate and on a conventional oak substrate to compare, yield, sensory attributes, and metabolite production. P. ostreatus showed no significant differences in yield or biological efficiency (p > 0.05), only sweetness (p = 0.022) differed significantly. H. erinaceus yield and efficiency were similar (p > 0.05), with greater second-flush yields in oak controls (p = 0.034) but no sensory differences (p > 0.05). G. lucidum performance was comparable across treatments (p > 0.05), yet triterpenoid content was reduced in pear substrates (p = 0.031). Results indicate P. calleryana biomass can sustain edible mushroom production without affecting yield or quality, while substrate composition influences bioactive metabolite synthesis, supporting invasive biomass valorization as a sustainable management strategy.

papers.title: Survival rates and challenges of mobilized tree planting seedlings in Wadla Woreda, Northeastern Ethiopia
papers.authors: Birhan Tadesse, Destaw Fentaw, Abdu Assen
papers.abstract: The main purpose of this study was to assess the level of seedling survival and associated challenges under community mobilization tree planting practices in Wadla Woreda, North Wollo Zone, Ethiopia. A descriptive survey design with a mixed approach was used, which included both quantitative and qualitative data collected from households, leaders of kebeles, development agents, and forestry experts. Primary data was gathered through questionnaires, interviews, focus groups, and transect walks, while secondary data, including reports and official records, was also reviewed. Based on transect walk data, the average seedling survival rate was 51.77% with a wide range of variations among the kebeles. Among sample kebeles, Meley recorded the highest (81.3%) survival rate, and Kuana registered the lowest (31.86%) survival rate. Woreda Agricultural Office records further showed that, seedling survival fluctuated between 2018 and 2022, declining from 89.4% in 2018 to 49.4% in 2020 before recovering to 84.6% in 2022. papers.title: Resource Rich but Risky Patches: Primary Productivity Triggers Intraguild Predation of Insects by Livestock in Oak Savannas
papers.authors: Álvaro Gaytán, Tara Canelo, Carlos Pérez‐Izquierdo, Raúl Bonal
papers.abstract: Theoretical models on intraguild predation (predation among organisms within the same trophic level, intraguild predation) assume a spatially heterogeneous primary productivity. Hence, resource-rich patches could attract both predators and prey, yet prey may suffer higher predation rates. This theoretical framework can be extended to antagonistic, size‑asymmetric interactions among herbivores in which negative effects arise not only from predation but also from other non‑trophic mechanisms. We analyzed antagonistic interactions driven by primary productivity among oak-defoliating Lepidoptera and livestock in Iberian oak savannas. Caterpillars defoliate oak canopies, but exclusion experiments have shown that free-range livestock predate/trample soil-pupating Lepidoptera. We used fine-scale multispectral imagery to assess the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) of oak canopies and surrounding pasture. Then, we tracked the visits of GPS-collared sheep in each tree of the study site, where we sampled oak-defoliating Lepidoptera caterpillars. papers.title: Bio-based nanoparticles for pesticide applications: a comprehensive review
papers.authors: Irianto Irianto, Nicky Rahmana Putra, Yustisia Yustisia, Izhar Khairullah, Syahrial Abdullah
papers.abstract: The effectiveness of conventional chemical pesticides has been increasingly undermined by pest resistance, environmental contamination, and non-target toxicity. Nano-enabled biopesticides have appeared as a promising alternative to enhance efficacy while reducing ecological risks. This review aims to critically evaluate recent advances in nanotechnology-based biopesticides, with emphasis on biopolymer, protein, and plant-derived nano formulations. Chitosan nanoparticles showed strong performance in dsRNA and essential-oil delivery, achieving 2.5-fold higher uptake, 60–67% pest mortality, and up to 96% gene silencing. Cellulose nanocrystal emulsions and alginate carriers enhanced stability and pathogen suppression by >70% while keeping plant compatibility. Protein-based systems, particularly zein nanoparticles, reduced LC50 values by 40–60% with minimal non-target toxicity. Across systems, nano formulation improved penetration, UV stability (2–10×), and controlled release. Nano-enabled biopesticides significantly enhance the efficiency and durability of biological active agents. However, challenges stay in large-scale field validation, environmental fate assessment, and regulatory h

papers.title: Insect-resistant rice and Metarhizium anisopliae sustain the brown planthopper susceptibility through AMPK-mediated lipid redistribution
papers.authors: Kai Lin, Yutao Hu, Guy Smagghe, Wenqing Zhang
papers.abstract: The brown planthopper (BPH), Nilaparvata lugens, rapidly overcomes host resistance and develops insecticide resistance, undermining sustainable rice pest control. Here, we show that combining insect-resistant rice IR36 with the entomopathogenic fungus Metarhizium anisopliae CQMa421 provides durable suppression of BPH under laboratory conditions. Across multiple generations, chemical insecticides drove resistance and host adaptation, whereas M. anisopliae maintained susceptibility. Combined exposure redistributed lipids by reducing diacylglycerol (DAG) and adenosine triphosphate (ATP) in the fat body and ovary while increasing DAG in the hemolymph, thereby prioritizing humoral immunity. This redistribution was mediated by AMPK activation in the fat body, which inhibited insulin signaling and lipid catabolism while limiting detoxification and reproduction. AMPK-mediated energy reallocation sustained BPH sensitivity to both resistant rice and fungal infection. Integrating plant resistance with microbial biocontrol therefore suppresses host adaptation and delays resistance evolution, offering a sustainable pest management strategy.

papers.title: 2. Death and Surveillance on Jim Crow Land
High prevalence of a honeybee-associated virus in wild bees in protected areas across Europe
papers.authors: Morgan A. Morrison, James A. O’Rourke, Tesni Houlston, Susie Topple, Gabrielle McLaughlin
papers.source: OpenAlex / Proceedings of the Royal Society B Biological Sciences
papers.abstract: Emerging diseases contribute to global biodiversity losses by causing local population declines and, with other stressors, increasing extinction risk. Protected areas are central to conservation efforts, yet they remain vulnerable to pathogen spillover and resultant impacts of emergent disease. We examined the extent and drivers of potential pathogen spillover from managed honeybees to wild bees across European grasslands in protected areas. Deformed wing virus B (DWV-B), a honeybee-associated virus, was found in all wild bee species tested (45% prevalence). Wild bee DWV prevalence was linked to the prevalence of DWV in honeybees and the abundance of bumblebees, while viral load in wild bees was associated with higher viral loads in honeybees. These findings indicate that pathogen spillover from managed bees might undermine the conservation value of protected areas. Our results suggest that proactive management is needed to reduce pathogen transmission and conserve the biodiversity these areas are intended to protect.

papers.title: Wolbachia dominance and host-form-consistent geographic structuring of the Culex pipiens complex microbiome across the Republic of Korea
papers.authors: Jeong-Hyeon Lee, Hee-Il Lee, Hyung-Wook Kwon
papers.abstract: Mosquito microbiomes are shaped by host genetic background and by the environment, but separating the two in wild populations is difficult, particularly when a single endosymbiont dominates the sequenced community. We present the first nationwide, complex-specific survey of the Culex pipiens complex microbiome in the Republic of Korea: 16S rRNA gene (V3–V4) amplicon sequencing of 29 pools of the two Korean host forms, Cx. pipiens pallens (cpp) and Cx. pipiens form molestus (cpm), collected between 1 and 15 August 2022 from 23 sites in 22 surveillance regions. Wolbachia accounted for 45.1% of the bacterial community on average (up to 94.7% in individual pools) and set the first axis of abundance-weighted ordinations. Beneath this dominance, mosquitoes from Jeju Island and from the mainland harbored distinct bacterial communities, differing in composition, phylogenetic diversity and evenness. papers.title: Criminal Liability for Violations of the Quarantine Regime in State Border Areas and at Border Crossing Points: Legal Issues and Challenges
papers.authors: Dorj Gandavaa, Vaanchig Javkhlantsogt, Khulan Myagmarjav
papers.source: OpenAlex / Advances in Social Sciences Research Journal
papers.abstract: Ensuring the security of Mongolia’s state borders and the effective organization of border protection activities are influenced by various social, economic, political, and epidemiological factors. Among these, the emergence and spread of particularly dangerous infectious diseases affecting humans, livestock, and wildlife constitute a significant challenge, particularly in the context of Mongolia’s traditional nomadic livestock husbandry and distinctive natural and climatic conditions. The outbreak of such diseases may necessitate the implementation of quarantine regimes and specific restrictions at designated sections of the state border. However, violations of established restrictions, regulations, instructions, and legal requirements may occur when individuals prioritize personal interests over public safety and collective welfare. Such violations can undermine the effectiveness of disease prevention and control measures and create additional challenges for state border security. papers.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Psychological characteristics could significantly impact applications for cosmetic surgery as well as precognition and satisfaction with surgery. The present study aimed to investigate the relationship between perfectionism, early maladaptive schemas, attachment styles, and body image concern by the mediating role of self-esteem in cosmetic surgery applicants. Methods: This was a predictive correlational study. A sample size of 400 women was selected based on Klein’s model (2016). The required data were collected by Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale (RSES) (1989), Multidimensional Perfectionism Scale (MPS), Young Schema Questionnaire (YSQ-S3), Adult Attachment Scale (AAS), and Body Image Concern Inventory (BICI), and analyzed using Pearson correlation coefficient and structural equations in SPSS and AMOS. papers.authors: Armin Sljivo, Haris Vukas, Muhamed Djedovic, Lana Lekic, Amina Tawil
papers.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Minimally invasive coronary artery bypass grafting (MICS CABG) via left anterior thoracotomy has emerged as a less invasive alternative to conventional open sternotomy (OPEN CABG), offering potential benefits in perioperative outcomes and complication rates. Objective. The aim of this study was to compare procedural characteristics, ventilation duration, drainage volumes, and postoperative complications between MICS CABG and OPEN CABG in a single-center cohort in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Methods. This retrospective cross-sectional study included 262 patients who underwent surgical revascularization between January 2019 and June 2023. Results. MICS CABG was associated with a shorter median procedure time (2.5 vs. 3.5 hours, p<0.001) and reduced mechanical ventilation duration (11.0 vs. 14.0 hours, p<0.001). Although ICU stay was similar (3.0 days, p=0.001), total hospitalization was shorter for MICS CABG (6.0 vs. 7.0 days, p<0.001). papers.abstract: Phyllophaga sp. is a pest that causes various types of damage to crops and economic losses. One control alternative is biological control, such as the use of entomopathogenic fungi that cause infections and death in various insects of economic interest. The objective of this research was to molecularly identify three strains of the entomopathogenic fungus Metarhizium, select those with the greatest pathogenic capacity against white grubs [Phyllophaga sp.], and with viability for mass reproduction and formulation as a bioinsecticide. The three strains belong to the species M. anisopliae, with strains Ma70 and Ma2 showing greater pathogenicity. They were reproduced in vitro and in rice to determine their commercial potential. Conidia production by both strains [2–3 × 10⁸] was lower than the target production [1 × 10¹⁰]; therefore, future research should focus on increasing conidia production in solid substrates.

papers.authors: Leon Marshall, John S. Ascher, Robert James Whittaker, Michael C. Orr, Alice Catherine Hughes
papers.abstract: Islands account for a disproportionate share of global biodiversity 1 , yet insects, including invaluable pollinators such as bees 2 , remain underrepresented in island biogeography research 3 . Here we present a global checklist of island bees, recording 4,147 species across 305 islands. Although islands comprise only about 6% of the Earth’s land area, they support around 20% of known global bee diversity, and 42% of insular species are endemic, making up around 8% of all known bee species. Island bee species richness peaks at mid-latitudes (at least in the Northern Hemisphere), mirroring continental trends 4 . Native richness increases with island area and declines with isolation, consistent with patterns in other taxa 5 . The strength of island species–area relationships varies among biomes and is steepest in Mediterranean-type systems, which also support disproportionately high bee richness relative to flowering plant diversity. The number of endemic species is highest on large tropical islands, reflecting extensive in situ diversification. Methods This study integrated leaf micromorphology, physiological and biochemical profiling, transcriptomics, and metabolomics to elucidate the coordinated defense architecture of chestnut against O. ununguis . Leaf anatomical traits of six cultivars, comprising three resistant and three susceptible genotypes, were evaluated, while four representative cultivars were subjected to physiological-biochemical assays, widely targeted metabolomic profiling, and RNA sequencing before and 2 days after mite infestation. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) and linear mixed models (LMMs) were used to characterize co-expression patterns and metabolite-morphology associations. papers.abstract: Leaf damage classifiers are usually trained and evaluated on public images collected elsewhere, and their behaviour in a new orchard is rarely measured. We quantified this gap for peach leaves. Eleven ImageNet-pretrained convolutional backbones, each with and without a Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM), were trained on 1415 public leaves (six classes). They were evaluated, with photograph-grouped cross-validation and confidence intervals, on 182 leaves from 122 photographs taken in a commercial orchard (four classes). On the public hold-out set, macro-F1 ranged from 0.670 to 0.772, and the ranking of the best models was not resolved; CBAM brought no improvement (pooled change −0.009 to −0.001). Without retraining, mean orchard macro-F1 was 0.634, against 0.719 on the same four public classes, but only after masking the two classes absent from the orchard; without masking, one-third of the leaves were assigned to them. Label-free normalisation-statistics alignment did not help, whereas fine-tuning raised the mean macro-F1 to 0.72, and a few tens of labelled leaves sufficed to match zero-shot transfer. papers.title: Plant bioluminescence for sustainable horticulture: Living biosensors, crop sentinels and precision crop monitoring
papers.authors: Parbin Huda Baruah
papers.source: OpenAlex / Journal of Ecology and Conservation
papers.abstract: Bioluminescence, although frequently framed as an ecological curiosity of fireflies, marine macrofauna and glow-in-the-dark fungi, has become a real-world tool for understanding plant biology. Over many decades, firefly luciferase-based reporter systems have facilitated sensitive and quantitative measurements of gene expression, circadian rhythms and signalling in living plants. The ability to achieve bioluminescence within a single organism, where both luciferase and its substrate are produced on demand, has only recently been realised through the construction of bacterial, for example *Vibrio*, and fungal light-producing pathways. This transition is particularly relevant to agriculture and horticulture, where repeated, non-destructive monitoring can be achieved without external luciferin application. This article connects the molecular basis of different bioluminescence systems with their recent applications in crop and horticultural research. Particular focus is placed on autonomous reporters for defence hormones, pattern-triggered immunity and viral infection, sentinel plants for protected cultivation, high-throughput phenotyping and breeding, and lux-based microbial biosensors

papers.abstract: The predator-prey system comprising brown anoles and curly-tailed lizards provides an ecological case study for investigating population dynamics and informing conservation efforts. The paper considers a delay lizard population model that incorporates interspecific competition, intraguild predation, and the asymmetric dispersal of brown anoles. We analyse the stability of the equilibria and investigate the existence of delay-induced Hopf bifurcation. From 2017 through 2022, we evaluated Bacillus mycoides isolate J (BmJ; LifeGard WG; FRAC P06) alone and in rotation with conventional fungicides for grapevine downy mildew (Plasmopara viticola) and powdery mildew (Erysiphe necator) control near Geneva, New York, USA. papers.abstract: Nonpoint source (NPS) pollution from agricultural, urban, and silvicultural land uses constitutes the leading remaining cause of surface water quality impairment in the United States and a primary driver of aquatic biodiversity loss, eutrophication, and drinking water contamination globally. Best management practices (BMPs) represent the primary technical and regulatory mechanism for NPS pollution control, encompassing a broad array of structural, vegetative, and managerial practices designed to reduce pollutant generation, transport, and delivery at the field, farm, and watershed scales. papers.authors: Rêve Dagher, Myriam Kessari, Nicolas Faysse, Leïla Temri, Faten Khamassi
papers.source: OpenAlex / Journal of Innovation Economics & Management
papers.abstract: This paper examines how the reactivation of neglected and underutilised species can constitute a form of innovation within agri-food regimes structured by strong lock-ins. Focusing on Tunisia’s dominant Deglet Noor variety, it analyses how regime-level lock-ins constrain the reactivation and scaling of local date varieties in Kebili. Drawing on 48 semi-structured interviews and documentary analysis, the paper identifies interacting agronomic, technological, market, governance and socio-cognitive lock-ins and shows how they reinforce one another along the value chain. Policy bias, infrastructures calibrated to Deglet Noor, and downstream price and investment incentives favour sorting-gap Deglet Noor products and crowd out local date production, processing and demand formation. Reactivating local date varieties involves recombining devalued resources and know-how with contemporary market and organisational arrangements. This process can be conceptualised as an innovation by reactivation. The analysis identifies the mechanisms that must be loosened for this pathway to scale. JEL Codes: Q16, Q18, O33, O38

papers.abstract: Abstract Bogong moths ( Agrotis infusa ) migrate biannually up to 1,000 km between their breeding areas and geographically restricted aestivation sites in the Australian Alps 1,2 . These moths navigate towards their distant goal using the stars as a compass 3 but navigate correctly even when the stars are obscured by clouds 3 , suggesting that their magnetic sense 4 probably harnesses the Earth’s magnetic field as a compass. papers.abstract: Late blight of potato, caused by Phytophthora infestans , is the most significant and dangerous disease of potatoes, leading to annual losses of billions of dollars worldwide. Two Trichoderma strains were investigated for their use as biological control organisms of this disease under both in vitro and greenhouse environments. On the basis of these results, the Trichoderma virens strain AY154945 Ir. 11 presented a more specific response to P. infestans than did the other strain AY154931, a T. koningii Ir. 502 strain. papers.title: From shade to sustenance: tree species in home and domestic gardens
papers.authors: Lucian Dincă, Cristinel Constandache, Adrian George Peticilă, Iulian Alexandru Bratu, Gabriel Murariu
papers.abstract: Introduction Home and domestic gardens are multifunctional systems that support biodiversity, food security, sustainable resource use, and human well-being. However, a comprehensive synthesis of tree species associated with these gardens and their ecological and socioeconomic contributions remains necessary. This review aimed to characterize research trends and synthesize the available evidence on tree species in home and domestic gardens worldwide. Methods A two-stage approach was applied, combining bibliometric analysis of publications retrieved from the Scopus and Web of Science databases for the period 1978–2024 with a qualitative review of the identified literature. The bibliometric dataset comprised 486 records. The qualitative synthesis examined four thematic areas, including tree species diversity, their uses, and their contributions to ecosystem services. papers.title: A fine-grained multitrophic biodiversity and environmental dataset for understanding global change impacts in drylands
papers.authors: Ana Morales‐González, Walter Ralph Jubber, Daniela Abegg, Dominik M. Behr, Tharina L. Bird
papers.abstract: Abstract Drylands harbour unique biodiversity that is increasingly threatened by climatic extremes and ongoing global change. Yet, biodiversity data, particularly for terrestrial soil invertebrates, remain extremely scarce. Here, we present a fine-grained multitrophic biodiversity and environmental database from the southern Kalahari, South Africa, comprising twelve interoperable datasets collected since 2023 across a study area of 7,294 ha spanning contrasting macrohabitats and land-use types. The core dataset contains abundance records for 394 above- and below-ground invertebrate species and morphospecies, collected through monthly live trapping. Complementary datasets include invertebrate biomass, vegetation composition, camera-trap records of 39 vertebrate species, more than 5.2 million soil temperature and moisture measurements, and spatial metadata. Shared spatial and temporal identifiers enable integrated analyses across trophic levels, environmental conditions, and spatial scales. The resource provides a growing baseline for investigating species activity patterns and biodiversity responses to land use, climatic variability, and global change in dryland ecosystems.
